react_result.final_narrative_text: A multi-paradigm metabolomics enrichment analysis of 10 differentially abundant metabolites revealed a single dominant biological signal with exceptional cross-paradigm consensus. Tryptophan metabolism — spanning the KEGG pathway hsa00380, the WikiPathways pathway WP:WP465 'Tryptophan metabolism', and the Reactome module R-HSA-209931 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' — emerged as the unambiguous winner. Six of the ten input compounds are direct tryptophan metabolites: L-tryptophan (C00078), tryptamine (C00398), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). MetaboAnalystR PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00380 first with p = 5.41 × 10⁻⁹, mummichog (m/z-direct network analysis) ranked 'Tryptophan metabolism' first with p = 0.003, and RaMP multi-DB ORA placed KEGG:map00380 and WP:WP465 as its top two hits (FDR = 3.4 × 10⁻¹⁵ and 4.1 × 10⁻¹⁵ respectively). A reconcile_inchikey pass confirmed all 10 inputs are structurally distinct (10 unique InChIKey block-14 clusters, zero conflicts). The three remaining inputs — 3-aminopropionaldehyde (C05665), 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid (C05947), and 4-hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677) — contributed to secondary hits in histidine/β-alanine metabolism (mummichog rank 1 and 6, p = 0.037 and 0.044) and retinol metabolism (mummichog rank 4, p = 0.044) but are not supported by ORA, indicating they are peripheral rather than driver compounds. Molybdate (C00150) did not enrich significantly in any paradigm, consistent with its role as a cofactor rather than a pathway substrate. The driver signal is the tryptophan → serotonin/melatonin axis and the tryptophan → kynurenine branch (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid). Treatment-induced perturbation of this pathway would affect neuroactive amine synthesis (biogenic amines WP:WP550, FDR = 3.98 × 10⁻⁸), neurotransmitter homeostasis (WP:WP4220, FDR = 6.9 × 10⁻⁸), and de novo NAD⁺ biosynthesis through the kynurenine branch (WP:WP4210, FDR = 6.9 × 10⁻⁸).

react_result.final_narrative_text: A multi-paradigm metabolomics enrichment analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites identified a single dominant biological signal with exceptional cross-paradigm consensus: tryptophan metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA placed KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as its top hit with FDR = 3.4 × 10⁻¹⁵ and six input compounds mapping to that pathway. The same pathway in WikiPathways (WP:WP465) was the second-ranked hit (FDR = 4.1 × 10⁻¹⁵). MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed this with KEGG:hsa00380 ranking first (p = 5.41 × 10⁻⁹). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis placed Tryptophan metabolism first with p = 0.0015 and an overlap of 13 out of 14 pathway compounds. Reactome REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) ranked third in RaMP (FDR = 3.59 × 10⁻⁸) with three compounds matching: L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin. WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production) ranked seventh in RaMP (FDR = 6.9 × 10⁻⁸) and confirms 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid as a member of the kynurenine branch. The driver signal is the tryptophan to serotonin and melatonin biosynthetic axis, consistent across ORA and network-based paradigms.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: A multi-paradigm metabolomics enrichment analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites identified a single dominant biological signal with exceptional cross-paradigm consensus: tryptophan metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA placed KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as its top hit with FDR = 3.4 × 10⁻¹⁵ and six input compounds mapping to that pathway. The same pathway in WikiPathways (WP:WP465) was the second-ranked hit (FDR = 4.1 × 10⁻¹⁵). MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed this with KEGG:hsa00380 ranking first (p = 5.41 × 10⁻⁹). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis placed Tryptophan metabolism first with p = 0.0015 and an overlap of 13 out of 14 pathway compounds. Reactome REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) ranked third in RaMP (FDR = 3.59 × 10⁻⁸) with three compounds matching: L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin. WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production) ranked seventh in RaMP (FDR = 6.9 × 10⁻⁸) and confirms 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid as a member of the kynurenine branch. The driver signal is the tryptophan to serotonin and melatonin biosynthetic axis, consistent across ORA and network-based paradigms.
